texts.preamble: Nirmal Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2020 Author: Vishnu Pratap Singh Chauhan Bench: Vishnu Pratap Singh Chauhan High Court Of Madhya Pradesh : Jabalpur Cr.R. No.37/2020 (Nirmal Sen Vs.State of M.P.) Jabalpur, Dated 09/01/20120
texts.facts: It is difficult for him to appear before the trial Court and prays to exempt the applicant from surrendering before the trial Court or Police and further prays to hear this revision in absence of surrendering the applicant before the trial Court. Perused the documents filed along with this revision specially the order sheets of the appellate Court. The applicant may surrender on the next day of the judgment or other day i.e. within ten days. It cannot be presumed that the appellant was enlarged on bail- bonds for ten days. 3. The case of prosecution, in short, is that the applicant is the person who was nominated by the Hindustan Lever Limited Company under Sub-section (2) of Section 17 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'PFA Act') to bear responsibility on behalf of the company for any offence under the PFA Act. Company prepared Vanaspati Ghee, Khajoor Brand and it was kept in the godown of Lipton India Ltd. H.D. Dubey, the then Food Inspector of District Flying Squade, Jabalpur went to the godown of Lipton India Limited where he found stock of Dalda Vanaspati Khajoor Brand Ghee kept in a cartoon. He after purchasing the products and after completing the formalities, sent the same for examination to the Public Analyst and after receiving report another sample was sent to Central Food Laboratory (hereinafter referred to 'CFL'). In these packets, Food Inspector also found that there was no declaration of label, batch, number, month and year of packing as provided under Rule 32 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. CFL found that melting point of the Vanaspati Ghee was higher than the normal range 31 to 41 degree Centigrade. In this respect found the Vanaspati Ghee adulterate and misbranding. After completion of whole process submitted a complaint against the company and applicant along with 26 persons. 4. Later on, the matter travelled upto Hon'ble Supreme Court on the ground that the person who is nominated by the company i.e. Hindustan Lever Limited, is responsible for the offence under the provisions of PFA Act. 5. The applicant remained absent before the Court of JMFC. It may be due to lost of sight because the case was pending before the trial Court since 1989. The applicant raised this lacuna in appeal and prayed therein to acquit him on the ground that Company-Hindustan Lever Limited has not been convicted in this case to which applicant is a nominated person for business affairs, however, learned appellate Court has not properly discussed this fact in para-31 of its judgment.
texts.arguments: It is also submitted by learned senior counsel that the applicant is facing a serious ailment, in general language suffering from prostate cancer with stricture urethra and undergone multiple cystoscopies and dilation. Rule 48 of High Court of Madhya Pradesh Rules, 2008 reads as under : "48. A memorandum of appeal or revision petition against conviction, except in cases where the sentence has been suspended by the Court below, shall contain a declaration to the effect that the convicted person is in custody or has surrendered after the conviction. Where the sentence has been so suspended, the factum of such suspension and its period shall be stated in the memorandum of appeal or revision petition, as also in the application under Section 389 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. . " 4 Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Vivek Rai and another Vs. High Court of Jharkhand, (2015) 12 SCC 86, clearly explained that in exceptional cases where the applicant is suffering from some grievous diseases and admitted in the hospital, revision can be entertained. Rule 48 of High Court of Madhya Pradesh, 2008 is pari materia with Rule 159 of the Jharkhand High Court Rules. Section 17 (1) (a) (b) reads as under : Nirmal Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189924179/ 5 "17. Offences by companies.-- (1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company -- (a) (i) the person, if any, who has been nominated under sub-section (2) to be in charge of, and responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company (hereafter in this section referred to as the person responsible), or (ii) where no person has been so nominated, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company; and (b) the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly: Provided that nothing contained in this sub- section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge and that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence." On bare perusal of the provisions of above section, if any product manufactured by the company found to be adulterated, the company as well as nominated person shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence described in Section 17(1) of the PFA Act. 7. The applicant clearly raised objection before learned appellate Court that learned trial Court has not convicted the company-Hindustan Lever Limited, therefore, the appellant being nominated person of the company, could not be held guilty of any offence if company is not held guilty. 8. If the company-Hindustan Lever Limited is acquitted of the charges, the said benefit will also directly go to the applicant.
